stories.headline: 2026-27 NBA season preview: Rankings, predictions, odds
stories.summary: Here's everything you need to know for all 30 NBA teams for the season, including storylines, stats and predictions ahead of opening night.
stories.body:
Welcome back to the NBA. Just in case you didn't hear:

Giannis Antetokounmpo is (finally) in Miami; Jaylen Brown (stunningly) is in Philadelphia; Ja Morant (somewhat stunningly) is in Portland; Kawhi Leonard is back in Toronto (it took a bit); LaMelo Ball is joining forces with Anthony Edwards in Minnesota's backcourt (it might take a bit); and the Lakers got a new lob threat for Luka Doncic (it worked last time): those major moves, plus the addition of a deep 2026 rookie class.

Oh. And a 41-year-old legend defying Father Time changed coasts, setting up the league's newest superteam, a major conference shift and potentially one of the most exciting seasons in recent history. Got all that?

On the eve of opening night, ESPN's NBA insiders and analysts are breaking down the storylines and stars that will shape 2026-27 and the run through the postseason.

Note: Team rankings are based on where members of our panel (ESPN's Jamal Collier, Michael C. Wright, Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Brian Windhorst, Ben Golliver, Ramona Shelburne, Kris Rhim, Baxter Holmes and Anthony Slater) think teams belong heading into this season.

Jump to a team:

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI

CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GS

HOU | IND | LAC | LAL | MEM

MIA | MIL | MIN | NO | NY

OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX | POR

SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS

1. Oklahoma City Thunder

Schedule | Roster | Best bet | Offseason recap

Chances to make the playoffs: 99.9%

Projected wins: 60.7

Biggest thing we'll be talking about this season: The Thunder still have arguably the NBA's deepest roster despite the departures of a trio of championship-winning role players (Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins) via a series of salary-shedding summer trades. Back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's supporting cast is loaded with talent, starting with All-NBA sidekicks Chet Holmgren and Jalen Williams. Cason Wallace, Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain are talented young players to whom the Thunder are eager to give more minutes. Rookie first-rounders Aday Mara and Bennett Stirtz both impressed during the preseason, but it will be difficult for them to earn immediate regular roles because OKC's rotation is so crowded. -- Tim MacMahon

Biggest strength: Oklahoma City has the league's top-ranked defense by a significant margin the last two seasons. The departure of Dort is a hit, but the Thunder still have a trio of recent All-Defensive selections (Wallace, Williams and Alex Caruso) to harass opposing perimeter stars. Holmgren is the most dominant defensive force in the league other than a certain Frenchman in San Antonio. The Thunder's ability to create turnovers fuels Oklahoma City's offense, and that aspect of the game should be upgraded with an increasing role for Wallace, last season's steals leader, and Williams' return to health. -- MacMahon

Biggest weakness: Rebounding is the biggest nit to pick with Oklahoma City, which ranked 22nd in the league with a 49.0% rebounding rate last season. The Thunder typically start a big lineup with a pair of 7-footers (Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein), but one blemish with the roster is that the size thins out at power forward behind Holmgren, whose lack of bulk is occasionally exposed in battles for rebounds. -- MacMahon

Bold prediction: The Thunder finish second -- not first -- in defensive rating. Oklahoma City led the league in this stat by wide margins in the last two seasons, finishing 2.5 points ahead of second place in 2024-25 and 2.4 points ahead of second place in 2025-26. But the Thunder lost Dort over the summer and will now rely on more defensive targets -- McCain and the young guys -- than in previous seasons, at the same time that Victor Wembanyama's Spurs could surpass them for the top spot on the defensive leaderboard. -- Zach Kram

Number to watch: 33%. In the 2024-25 regular season, when the Thunder went 68-14 and set a point differential record en route to the championship, they won 83% of their games. In 2025-26, counting both regular season and playoffs, they did slightly better by winning 84% of their games -- if you don't count their 4-8 record against the Spurs. But those 12 games at a 33% winning percentage -- 1-4 in the regular season, 3-4 in the conference finals -- were the most important of the Thunder's season, as they prevented Oklahoma City from returning to the Finals. -- Kram

Fantasy nugget: Wallace recorded 150 steals in 77 games last season despite averaging just 26.6 MPG. With Dort and Joe gone, he could see additional playing time. Wallace is being drafted just inside 150, making him particularly appealing for managers targeting steals late in category leagues. Increased minutes could also improve his 3-point production, although his scoring remains limited. -- Eric Moody

What Bobby Marks is watching: The Clippers. For a second consecutive season, Oklahoma City could have a lottery pick despite playing deep into the playoffs. The Thunder have two of the most favorable first-round picks of the Clippers, Denver (if 6-30) and their own. The Thunder also have a first from San Antonio if it falls between 17 and 30. The first from the Clippers was acquired as part of the James Harden trade with Philadelphia. The BPI projects LA to have the league's fifth-worst record.

BPI first-round projection: No. 5 (via LAC), No. 24 (via DEN), No. 29 (via SA)

2. San Antonio Spurs

Schedule | Roster | Best bet | Offseason recap

Chances to make the playoffs: 99.9%

Projected wins: 59.1

Biggest thing we'll be talking about this season: At least early on, San Antonio's experimentation with three-guard lineups featuring De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle will generate most of the conversations concerning the Spurs. But other interesting lineups could be on the horizon with Spurs coach Mitch Johnson explaining, "That's just part of natural evolution that will take some time. But it's time to also push forward appropriately." Victor Wembanyama serves as the linchpin driving potential innovation in San Antonio. "Victor allows you to think outside the box in almost any way you want to," Johnson explained. -- Michael C. Wright

Biggest strength: Fox, Harper and Castle represent arguably the most talented backcourt trio in the league, and the overall roster is teeming with so much depth the Spurs will be forced to make difficult decisions regarding lineups. If San Antonio opts to start the guard trio regularly, its bench will be led by Julian Champagnie, who set a franchise record for made 3-pointers last season, and Keldon Johnson, the reigning NBA Sixth Man of the Year. -- Wright

Biggest weakness: Outside of Wembanyama, free agent addition Tobias Harris and backup center Luke Kornet, San Antonio is relatively thin in the frontcourt. First-round pick Tarris Reed Jr. has shown promise throughout training camp and the preseason and might have a chance to fill in at center when frontcourt depth is thinned by injuries or rest days for Wembanyama or Kornet. -- Wright

Bold prediction: Wembanyama records the NBA's first quadruple-double since David Robinson in 1994, and just the fifth in recorded history. I also made this prediction last season and didn't come all that close to hitting, but I trust Wembanyama enough to try again. He has already reached double-digit assists three times in his career and double-digit blocks three times (counting playoffs), so he just needs to combine those achievable feats in the same game. -- Kram

Number to watch: 17.0. The Spurs posted a plus-17.0 net rating with Wembanyama on the floor last year, per NBA Advanced Stats. That was the second-best mark among all rotation players, and the only one in the top six that didn't belong to a Thunder player: Alex Caruso led the league in this stat, followed by Wembanyama, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Chet Holmgren, Ajay Mitchell and Isaiah Hartenstein. -- Kram

Fantasy nugget: Castle averaged 16.7 PPG, 5.3 RPG and 7.4 APG last season, leading the Spurs in assists despite sharing the backcourt with Fox. He also averaged 8.9 assists per 36 minutes, up from 5.5 as a rookie. Harper's development could create more competition for touches, but Castle's rebounding and playmaking make him an appealing target at his ADP. -- Moody

What Bobby Marks is watching: Keldon Johnson's next contract. The reigning Sixth Man of the Year appeared in all 83 games last season (including the NBA Cup title game), setting the record for most points in a season by a reserve. But in the playoffs, Johnson reached double-digit points in just five of San Antonio's 16 games. Johnson is entering the final year of his contract and, through June 30, can extend for up to four seasons. With year one of Wembanyama's rookie extension set to begin next season, San Antonio is $9 million below the luxury and $16 million under the first apron.

BPI first-round projection: No. 14 (via ATL). Note: From the Dejounte Murray trade, San Antonio has an unprotected Atlanta first. The Spurs' own 2027 first will go to Sacramento or Oklahoma City.

3. New York Knicks

Schedule | Roster | Best bet | Offseason recap

Chances to make the playoffs: 97.7%

Projected wins: 51.7

Biggest thing we'll be talking about this season: How this team handles being the defending champion. For as much pressure as the Knicks faced within New York when breaking the 53-year drought, they'll face a different type of pressure on the road to repeating. Contracts for two key players, Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart, along with the competition in the East ramping up will have many wondering if the Knicks will go for it in the regular season or play the long game. -- Vincent Goodwill

Biggest strength: Jalen Brunson has emerged into one of the steadiest leaders in the NBA and one of the most trusted in the clutch. If the Knicks go through regular-season turbulence, expect Brunson to address it internally and keep a cool head externally. If there's turbulence in a game, count on Brunson to play smart basketball with the rock in his hands. Now that he has cemented himself as a champion, he can play with a little extra arrogance knowing that he has conquered every challenge in front of him. -- Goodwill

Biggest weakness: Frontcourt depth. There will be times Mike Brown places OG Anunoby at small-ball center, although smart money says it won't happen too much. Losing Mitchell Robinson to Boston is a big blow to New York's rim protection and offensive rebounding, as he had his fingerprints on more than a few wins in critical situations last year. Will Andre Drummond -- a different type of center as far as skill set -- be able to fill the void in his own way? And will Towns and Drummond be reliable enough defensively for the long haul? -- Goodwill

Bold prediction: The Knicks win fewer regular-season games than in 2025-26. After a run to the Finals, the Knicks might take their foot off the pedal a bit in the regular season, and they benefited from excellent health that might not be repeatable (except by Mikal Bridges) this season. And with a stronger top-to-bottom Eastern Conference and the removal of tanking incentives, the Knicks could decline from 53 wins to a number lower in the 50s without compromising their status as favorites to return to the Finals. -- Kram

Number to watch: 14.9. The Knicks set a record with a plus-14.9 point differential in the playoffs, which was the highest mark for any champion in NBA history. Six of the seven previous leaders in this stat went on to repeat as champions the following season. -- Kram

Fantasy nugget: The Knicks ranked third in the NBA in team offensive rating (ORtg) last season with 119.8 points scored per 100 possessions, then they improved to first in playoffs ORtg with 120.4 PP100 against better competition. First-year head coach Brown's offensive system proved successful, and really ramped up when he started running the offense more through Towns as a distributor in the postseason. High-efficiency offenses are good for fantasy production in general, but for Towns specifically, a further adaptation of his postseason role could lead to career-best assist numbers that would round him into a top-15 fantasy prospect. -- Snellings

What Bobby Marks is watching: Will extensions talks (or lack thereof) become distractions? The Knicks made a decision to publicly announce that contract extensions will not be negotiated until later in the season. Since the NBA Finals concluded in June, Towns, Hart, Miles McBride and Tyler Kolek have been eligible to sign new deals.

BPI first-round projection: None (Note: The Knicks sent Brooklyn their unprotected first as part of the Mikal Bridges trade.)

4. Philadelphia 76ers

Schedule | Roster | Best bet | Offseason recap

Chances to make the playoffs: 88.3%

Projected wins: 47.5

Biggest thing we'll be talking about this season: Everything. If training camp was any indicator, there is no story too small to draw outsized attention with this team. Whether it was LeBron James' new mode of airborne transportation, Jaylen Brown's lack of interest in naming a pecking order for the new group or Joel Embiid rebutting a report about being late to practice, it is abundantly clear that every step Philadelphia takes will be chronicled and scrutinized. The talk will continue at that pitch until the Sixers show the team they are going to become. -- Dave McMenamin

Biggest strength: Top-level talent. With James, Brown, Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe, the Sixers have one of the best starting fives in the league. Brown is coming off a career season with the Boston Celtics in which he averaged 29 points, seven rebounds and five assists per game. Maxey was fifth in the league in scoring last year (28.3 points) and was named an All-Star in two of the past three seasons. Edgecombe averaged 16.0 points, 5.6 rebounds and 4.2 assists as a 20-year-old rookie. Embiid, when healthy, remains an offensive force. And James, despite being 41, is coming off yet another All-NBA season and playoff run in which he demonstrated he can still shoulder the load when the stakes are high. -- McMenamin

Biggest weakness: Chemistry. The Sixers rostered nine new players this season (including two-way contracts), and no matter how organized Philadelphia coach Nick Nurse might be, it will take time to round out his rotation and identify his ideal lineups. The second weakness is health -- not a unique obstacle for Philadelphia, but a pronounced one with Embiid missing 150 games in the last three seasons and Ariel Hukporti, a center signed in free agency to back Embiid up, going down with a season-ending Achilles tear in the preseason. -- McMenamin

Bold prediction: James scores the fewest points among the 76ers' starting five. James fell from 24.4 points in 2024-25 to 20.9 last season, tying his career low (with his rookie campaign). Brown, Maxey and Embiid all outscored him by 6-plus PPG and should do so again. So this prediction is really predicated on Edgecombe, who averaged 16 PPG as a rookie, slightly increasing his production while James' falls again -- which is eminently possible if James gets less playing time to stay fresh for the playoffs and takes on more of a distributor role because he's the best passer in this talented starting group. -- Kram

Number to watch: 55.8%. According to GeniusIQ, the 76ers' defense allowed a shot quality of 55.8% last season, meaning their opponents would have been expected to finish with a 55.8% effective field goal mark, based on factors like shot location and defender distance. That was the sixth-highest opponent shot quality in the league, behind only five tanking teams that all lost at least 56 games. In other words, Philadelphia allowed the easiest shots of any team that was trying to win games. -- Kram

Fantasy nugget: The addition of James and Brown this offseason limits the fantasy outlook for all of their players. Brown, James, Maxey, Edgecombe and, when healthy, Embiid are all proven fantasy producers with high ceilings. But when playing together, none of them can attain their typical usage or volume. The presence of so much talent, along with two strong distributors in James and Maxey, could have a positive effect on each player's efficiency. But ultimately, the capped volume also caps each individual's fantasy value. -- Snellings

What Bobby Marks is watching: Maxey's next contract. Will the 76ers star-studded lineup cost Maxey a significant payday next summer? Because he was named All-NBA last season, Maxey is eligible to sign a four-year, $304 million deal next summer if he was named All-NBA again. He would also become eligible to sign a five-year, $393 million super max extension in the 2028 offseason. (Maxey has played at least 65 games in three of his six seasons.)

BPI first-round projection: No. 25

5. Minnesota Timberwolves

Schedule | Roster | Best bet | Offseason recap

Chances to make the playoffs: 95.5%

Projected wins: 47.8

Biggest thing we'll be talking about this season: The backcourt fit. Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball -- from personality to play style to production -- form one of the most spectacular, captivating guard duos in recent NBA memory. They will draw eyeballs and generate a steady stream of highlights. But there's a reasonable question about how seamlessly they can fit. How well does Edwards, powering into his prime at 25, cede control of the offense to a true point guard? And can Ball sharpen his winning habits in a newer environment and now facing the greatest expectations of his career? -- Anthony Slater

Biggest strength: Pure talent and positional athleticism. The Wolves' perhaps forgotten man, Jaden McDaniels, had one of the more impressive first-round playoff performances in the league. He completely erased Nuggets guard Jamal Murray on the defensive end and scored 32 points in the closeout game without Edwards. At 26, McDaniels appears ready to become a two-way force on the wing. Minnesota is also planting Jonathan Kuminga, another highflyer entering his mid-20s, next to him in the starting lineup, while 7-3 Rudy Gobert (aging well at 34) looms behind as the protector. -- Slater

Biggest weakness: The weakened frontcourt in the matchups that matter. Victor Wembanyama, Nikola Jokic and the Isaiah Hartenstein-Chet Holmgren combination remain as playoff tests the Timberwolves must conquer. Gobert defended Jokic well last April but struggled against Wembanyama. But he had bulkier backup. To acquire Ball, they had to give up Julius Randle and Naz Reid, stripping away at one of the deepest frontcourts in the league. They did grab Kuminga on a $6 million bargain but might need a breakout season from him to quell concerns. -- Slater

Bold prediction: Minnesota finishes with its best offensive ranking and worst defensive ranking since trading for Gobert. To date, the Timberwolves' best offensive finish with Gobert is eighth and their worst defensive finish is eighth. But they downsized with the Ball trade, and now they simultaneously have their most electric offensive backcourt in years -- possibly ever -- and their weakest defensive rotation around ace defenders Gobert and McDaniels. -- Kram

Number to watch: 6,008. The Timberwolves' acquisition of Ball means they now have the No. 1 and No. 3 picks from the 2020 draft in their backcourt: Edwards and Ball, respectively. Both players are All-Stars with incredible shooting range and a flair for highlights in transition. But among other differences -- such as Edwards' two conference finals trips, contrasted with zero playoff games for Ball -- one important gap separates the players' NBA trajectories thus far: Edwards has played 6,008 more regular-season minutes than his new teammate. That's the equivalent of roughly 200 extra games at a starter's workload. -- Kram

Fantasy nugget: Ball averaged 20.1 points, 7.1 assists and 3.8 made 3s in just 28.0 minutes per game last season. He also played 72 games, including 56 straight to close the season. Edwards remains Minnesota's primary scorer, but Ball should have a significant playmaking role, making him especially valuable for assists in category leagues. His second-round draft cost is risky, though, given his extensive injury history. -- Moody

What Bobby Marks is watching: All-NBA and Edwards. Last season, Edwards failed to play 65 games to qualify for All-NBA honors despite averaging the third-most points per game in the league. Edwards also missed a chance at becoming supermax-eligible. He has another in 2026-27. If Edwards plays at least 65 games and is named MVP, All-NBA or Defensive Player of the Year this season, he will become eligible to sign a four-year, $304 million supermax extension next summer. The contract would keep him in a Timberwolves uniform through the 2031-32 season.

BPI first-round projection: None (Note: The Timberwolves sent Utah their 2027 first as part of the Rudy Gobert trade.

6. Boston Celtics

Schedule | Roster | Best bet | Offseason recap

Chances to make the playoffs: 97.2%

Projected wins: 51.3

Biggest thing we'll be talking about this season: The Jaylen Brown trade. The Celtics made a carefully considered decision to trade All-Star forward Brown to the 76ers, but the potential for that to backfire is still enormous. Just imagine the anger and outrage in Boston if the 2024 Finals MVP helps the 76ers win their first championship since 1983. While that worst-case scenario became more plausible when LeBron James joined Philadelphia on a veterans minimum contract, Boston should remain one of the East's top contenders after adding Paul George and Mitchell Robinson this summer. Jayson Tatum should be back to his All-NBA level form now that he's 18 months removed from his Achilles tear, and coach Joe Mazzulla has established a winning, high-effort culture that has delivered at least 56 wins in each of his four seasons. -- Ben Golliver

Biggest strength: 3-point shooting. Even though centers Neemias Queta and Mitchell Robinson are both non-shooters, Boston should once again boast strong spacing and an offensive system that generates a barrage of 3-point looks. After ranking fourth in 3-point attempts in 2025-26, the Celtics will likely climb even higher with Tatum and George leading the way as a high-volume shooting duo. Mazzulla's list of reliable marksmen also includes Payton Pritchard, Baylor Scheierman and Sam Hauser. -- Golliver

Biggest weakness: Free throw generation. After ranking last in free throw attempts in 2025-26, Boston must find new ways to get to the charity stripe. Its blockbuster summer trade only made this situation more dire: Brown ranked fifth leaguewide in free throw attempts last season, while George's free throw rate has dropped noticeably as he has progressed through his mid-30s. A healthy Tatum should draw more fouls than he did last season, and the Celtics would really benefit from the crafty Pritchard taking a step forward in this department. -- Golliver

Bold prediction: Robinson and Queta combine to produce the value of a top-five center. Advanced stats adore both Robinson and Queta, who score efficiently, play stalwart defense and do all the little things -- such as grab offensive rebounds and set sturdy screens -- that make them stand out in player value metrics. Neither player is an All-Star on his own, but their partnership could produce All-Star-caliber value in Mazzulla's system. -- Kram

Number to watch: 4. In all four of Mazzulla's seasons as Boston's coach, the Celtics have finished with a top-five offensive and defensive rating, per Cleaning the Glass. Only three other squads in that span have accomplished that feat: the 2023-24 Thunder, the 2024-25 Thunder and the 2025-26 Spurs. -- Kram

Fantasy nugget: The Celtics had led the NBA in 3-point attempts and 3-pointers made for two straight seasons before last season, when they finished fourth in attempts and third in makes. Their drop from 48.2 3PA/game in 2024-25 to 42.1 3PA/G last season was likely influenced by the injury absence of Tatum (9.1 3PA/G for last three seasons) for most of the season with the offense built more around Brown's more midrange game (5.7 3PA/G for last three seasons). But Tatum is back full time, and Brown was traded this offseason for George (8.0 3PA/G for the last eight seasons). Expect the Celtics as a team to bounce back to the league lead in 3-pointers, with all of their fantasy contributing shooters maximizing their 3-pointers made. -- Snellings

What Bobby Marks is watching: George's future. Does a strong season by George parlay into a new contract but at a lower salary? Including his $56.6 million player option next season, Boston is $6.7 million over the luxury tax and $16 million under the first apron. An option that would boost Boston's flexibility: George declines the option and re-signs at a lesser value but with more guaranteed years.

BPI first-round projection: No. 27

7. Detroit Pistons

Schedule | Roster | Best bet | Offseason recap

Chances to make the playoffs: 93.4%

Projected wins: 49.4

Biggest thing we'll be talking about this season: Cade Cunningham, as usual. He elevated himself into the MVP strata last season with a career year and still has room to grow as he enters Year 6. In the playoffs, he showed his shooting can go to another level, shooting over 40% from 3 in 14 games -- which might be the last step to a complete offensive package. He believes Detroit is being overlooked in the East with all the talent upgrades in the conference but assuming health, it's hard to envision Detroit falling back to the pack if Cunningham has a similar season. -- Golliver

Biggest strength: Continuity. Losing Isaiah Stewart and Tobias Harris is no small measure, and perhaps some toughness goes out the door. But having Cunningham, Ausar Thompson and Jalen Duren still making strides together will do wonders while many of the newly constructed teams have to get acclimated to each other. Will they be third again in defense? Hard to say. But J.B. Bickerstaff's system on that end will still be stingy, enabling this team to use its sweat equity to win its share of games. -- Golliver

Biggest weakness: Is too much being asked of Cunningham? It was on full display during the playoffs when defenses were able to load up on him and he had some high-turnover games. The front office didn't make a bold move to rectify that, even if it didn't hurt in the regular season. Expect Duren and Thompson to take on more responsibility to initiate offense. -- Goodwill

Bold prediction: Isaiah Joe receives Sixth Man of the Year votes. For four seasons in a row, Joe has made more than 40% of his 3s, and he looks like a new version of Malik Beasley for the Pistons. Beasley finished second in Sixth Man voting in his lone season in Detroit. -- Kram

Number to watch: 6. Along with Cunningham, Thompson and Duren seem like two of the Pistons' three great building blocks -- assuming Duren signs a long-term deal rather than taking the qualifying offer. That's why it's so notable, and so potentially concerning, that Thompson and Duren made six combined 3-pointers last season. -- Kram

Fantasy nugget: The Pistons brought in 28-year-old John Collins this offseason to replace 34-year-old Tobias Harris as the starting power forward. Collins is bigger, more explosive and a better finisher than Harris at this point in their respective careers. Collins showed in his days with the Hawks that he operates well as a finisher next to a dominant offense-creating point guard, setting single-season-bests of 21.6 PPG and 10.1 RPG next to Trae Young. This season, Collins will be playing off MVP candidate Cunningham, and could be a late-round fantasy sleeper with the potential to produce one of his best seasons. -- Snellings

What Bobby Marks is watching: Will Langdon be tempted to go all-in because of the expiring contracts? With the core of Cunningham, Thompson and Duren under contract for at least the next four seasons, Detroit has the tradable contracts and up to four first-round picks to make a big move. Duncan Robinson ($15.2 million), Collins ($17 million) and Joe ($11.3 million) either have a non-guaranteed salary next season or a team option. Since taking over as GM in June 2024, Langdon has made 11 trades. None have included the Pistons dealing their own first-round pick.

BPI first-round projection: No. 26

8. Denver Nuggets

Schedule | Roster | Best bet | Offseason recap

Chances to make the playoffs: 96.9%

Projected wins: 48.7

Biggest thing we'll be talking about this season: When Denver won the NBA title in 2023, it felt like it could be the beginning of a five-year championship contention window. After three straight early playoff exits, the pressure is mounting for Denver to give perennial MVP candidate Nikola Jokic another real shot at contention. The all-world big man is squarely in his prime and has said he'll sign the supermax extension if it's offered after the season, but each year the financial realities of the Nuggets' situation make it harder to surround him with championship-caliber depth. -- Ramona Shelburne

Biggest strength: The experience and consistency of the Nuggets' championship trio of Jokic, Jamal Murray and Aaron Gordon is still intact and still incredibly potent -- when healthy. Denver has a regular-season record of 125-51 (a 71.0% win rate) when those three play together. Last season they went 20-6: an elite record, but a painfully small number of games. -- Shelburne

Biggest weakness: The Nuggets' bench was a strength during their championship run, but that depth has slowly withered away each successive season as financial constraints have limited Denver's roster building. This offseason, Peyton Watson was the biggest roster casualty, as Denver ended up trading the young swingman they'd so carefully drafted and developed, rather than match the offer sheet he signed in Cleveland. None of this will help the devastating on/off splits that plague the Nuggets every time Jokic comes off the floor. Last year had an elite plus-10.8 net rating with Jokic, but a minus-6.5 net rating when he was off the court. -- Shelburne

Bold prediction: Jokic posts the largest on/off differential of his career. This will be a tall task for Jokic, who routinely posts the widest on/off differential in the league. But this is a bet on two factors, which are both realistic: First, Jokic will be as dominant as ever, just like he was last season before being waylaid by injury; and second, the Nuggets' bench will be more disastrous than usual without Jokic, due to the team's lack of depth and a reliance on Marvin Bagley III and Zeke Nnaji as backup bigs. -- Kram

Number to watch: 4. According to the advanced stat estimated plus-minus, only four Nuggets rate as above-average players at this point in their careers. To be fair, that quartet -- consisting of Jokic, Murray, Gordon and Cameron Johnson -- is generally way above-average. Jokic, for instance, is the second-most-valuable player in the league by EPM's reckoning, behind only Victor Wembanyama. -- Kram

Fantasy nugget: DeMar DeRozan averaged 18.4 PPG and 4.1 APG last season with the Kings, but he is expected to come off the bench in Denver. He should still have opportunities to score with the second unit, but his minutes could decline. He still offers scoring value, though his expected role off the bench makes him a player fantasy managers shouldn't reach for in drafts. -- Moody

What Bobby Marks is watching: The Nuggets acquired a 2031 unprotected first from Cleveland in the Watson sign-and-trade. That matters because it gives Denver the flexibility to trade either the Cavaliers' first or their own in 2031 (they can't trade both). The Nuggets have the $23 million expiring contract of Johnson as the possible centerpiece of any trade.

BPI first-round projection: None. Note: Denver's 2027 first (top-five protected) will go to the LA Clippers, Oklahoma City or Toronto.

9. Cleveland Cavaliers

Schedule | Roster | Best bet | Offseason recap

Chances to make the playoffs: 88.4%

Projected wins: 47.9

Biggest thing we'll be talking about this season: The Cavs made two big decisions this offseason and how they play out will largely define the season. They could've gone for big swings in getting involved in the pursuit of Giannis Antetokounmpo or Jaylen Brown but it likely would've cost them Evan Mobley. The front office still deeply believes in Mobley in the wake of a bit of a disappointing season, however. The other choice was the acquisition of Peyton Watson, which caused them to make a series of expensive trades and salary shedding moves. They believe Watson is on the verge of a breakout after he showed flashes in Denver last season. -- Brian Windhorst

Biggest strength: The Cavs have four starters who have been All-Stars (Mobley, Jarrett Allen, James Harden and Donovan Mitchell) plus Watson, who they believe is on his way to being an elite two-way wing. They believe this group, coming off a conference finals appearance, has enough firepower to win the East. -- Windhorst

The aftermath of the Leonard salary cap investigation has left the Clippers in a precarious position, with Ballmer suspended for one year and head of basketball operations Lawrence Frank out for six months. Does Trent Redden, who will oversee basketball operations until March, have autonomy to make significant roster changes? The Clippers have no available first-round picks to trade but do have the expiring contracts of Lopez, Jones, Strus, Dunn and Rui Hachimura.

BPI first-round projection: No. 20 (via TOR) (Note: Despite forfeiting five future picks, the Clippers still have a first-rounder in the 2027 draft: the least favorable of Denver (top-five protected) and Oklahoma City. That pick can be swapped for Toronto's.)

28. Brooklyn Nets

Schedule | Roster | Best bet | Offseason recap

Chances to make the playoffs: 0%

Projected wins: 25

Biggest thing we'll be talking about this season: How the Nets will try to win games after the new lottery rules completely shifted their long-term plans and will attempt to slow-play this rebuild. Mikel Brown Jr. was one of the top point guards selected in the 2026 draft, and he is arguably the most confident. He also is very young; hopefully by season's end, he will look like a franchise point guard. -- Goodwill

Biggest strength: As long as new additions Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr. are suiting up, the Nets won't lack thirsty offensive players. On his best day, Randle is a load to handle physically and a capable playmaker. Porter, we know, has no problem taking on the task of being a No. 1 option, liable to go on a heater at a moment's notice. Porter's future could be slightly murkier because he will be an unrestricted free agent after the season, but as long as he's around, account for both of them. -- Goodwill

Biggest weakness: It's hard to press the fast-forward button in just one season. There's just not a lot of top-level NBA talent down the roster. There is, however, a lot of opportunity. Remember, the Nets held onto all of their first-round picks in the 2025 draft and went through a lot of growing pains. -- Goodwill

Bold prediction: The Nets land their first player on the All-Star team since Kevin Durant. Brooklyn hasn't exactly been at the center of the NBA map since the Durant-Irving-Harden team disintegrated. But Porter was an All-Star contender last season, and he and Randle could make worthy cases this campaign, as both players put up solid regular-season stats. -- Kram

Number to watch: 72%. Egor Demin was by far the best of the Nets' rookies last season, averaging 10.3 points per game and a solid assist-to-turnover ratio while making 38.5% of his 3-pointers. That latter statistic is especially encouraging for a player with shooting questions entering the NBA. But Demin didn't find many ways to score other than 3-pointers, as 72% of his shot attempts last season were 3s. That was the 16th-highest rate out of 279 players with at least 1,000 minutes last season; the three immediately ahead of Demin were shooting specialists Klay Thompson, Gary Trent Jr. and Landry Shamet. -- Kram

Fantasy nugget: Fantasy sleepers watch for the Nets' young starting backcourt of rookie No. 5 draft pick Brown and last season's No. 8 selection Demin. Demin battled injuries for much of his rookie campaign and averaged roughly 10/3/3 in 52 games, but he showed flashes of all-around upside and proved himself "too good for summer league" this year while averaging 21.0 PPG, 4.3 APG and 2.3 SPG in 25.3 MPG in Las Vegas. Brown, meanwhile, showed flashes of his own this summer while averaging 16.7 PPG and 4.0 APG in 22.5 MPG. The rebuilding Nets should give their backcourt of the future plenty of minutes and an opportunity to produce fantasy-worthy stats this season. -- Snellings

What Bobby Marks is watching: Future draft assets. With no incentive to bottom out in the standings, would Brooklyn explore trades to improve the current roster but at the cost of future first-round picks? The Nets have nine tradable firsts and 19 seconds over the next seven seasons. They also have a $40.8 million expiring contract for Porter.

BPI first-round projection: No. 21 (via HOU), No. 28 (via NYK) (Note: The Rockets can swap firsts with the Nets. Brooklyn has an unprotected first from New York.)

29. Milwaukee Bucks

Schedule | Roster | Best bet | Offseason recap

Chances to make the playoffs: 0.1%

Projected wins: 26.3

Biggest thing we'll be talking about this season: Who stays and who goes? The Bucks are still a team in transition after trading their superstar over the summer. Every once in a while this season, you might catch a highlight and get reminded, "Oh yeah, that guy does play for the Bucks." Tyler Herro, Myles Turner, Kyle Kuzma and any of the other former Miami players: Are any of these players a part of the team's long-term future? Where does Kevin Porter Jr. fit in after finding a role with Milwaukee the past two seasons now that the team has added an influx of guards. Will Gary Trent Jr. play well enough to justify his contract? There could be a wide gap between how this roster looks at the beginning of the season and by the end. -- Collier

Biggest strength: Depth. Whatever buttons new coach Taylor Jenkins decides to push this season with his rotation, he should have one major benefit: a lot of NBA-level talent. The Bucks should have very few minutes without five competent NBA players on the floor, even if they do give a lot of time to their rookies. With a surplus of players acquired in the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade to add to a mix of talent already on the roster, the Bucks will be deep, if ill-fitting. On the right night, it could all add up to more than the sum of its parts. -- Collier

Biggest weakness: Identity. The Bucks have veterans trying to rebuild their value, veterans finally getting more playing time out of the shadow of a superstar, young players who are still finding their way and a pair of first-round draft picks who need to go through growing pains. Nearly everyone is capable of filling in some kind of role. But is there a coherent way to fit them all together? And how does that hold up on a nightly basis? -- Collier

Bold prediction: The Bucks trade multiple opening-night starters by the deadline. Milwaukee has been quiet on the trade market since moving Antetokounmpo, but that deal reoriented the Bucks' competitive timetable and gave them plenty of players who'd be better fits on win-now contenders. Turner, Herro, Kuzma, Jaime Jaquez Jr. and even young guard Ryan Rollins could all fit for this prediction. -- Kram

Number to watch: 11. For each of the past 11 seasons, Antetokounmpo led the Bucks in value over replacement player, per Basketball-Reference. That streak will come to an end this campaign after his offseason trade to Miami. -- Kram

Fantasy nugget: The Bucks are a team in a rebuild, and they just traded Antetokounmpo for a large quantity of players and draft picks. The end result is a squad with a lot of depth and an unclear distribution of minutes. The projected starting lineup to start the season has two players over 30 years old in Turner and Kuzma, and both have proved to be productive fantasy contributors when starting. However, if the team follows a typical rebuilding arc and falls far behind in the standings, do not be surprised if younger players such as Kasparas Jakucionis, Kel'el Ware and rookie Brayden Burries see their roles -- and their fantasy output -- increase as the season goes along. -- Snellings

What Bobby Marks is watching: The veterans. The Bucks added two future firsts and young players Ware, Jakucionis and Jaime Jaquez as part of the Antetokounmpo trade. But this roster remains full of players who no longer fit Milwaukee's timeline, including Herro (age 26), Kuzma (31), Turner (30), Trent (27) and Caris LeVert (32). Herro, LeVert and Kuzma are in the final year of their contracts and could be trade targets for contenders.

BPI first-round projection: None (Note: The Bucks sent New Orleans their own first as part of the Jrue Holiday trade. The least favorable first between Milwaukee and New Orleans will be sent to Atlanta if it falls outside the top five.)

30. Sacramento Kings

Schedule | Roster | Best bet | Offseason recap

Chances to make the playoffs: 0%

Projected wins: 21.7

Biggest thing we'll be talking about this season: Darius Acuff Jr.'s high-usage rookie season. The front office is in the middle stages of flipping this roster over entirely. General manager Scott Perry has added six players through the draft during his first two years on the job. That group will be prioritized, and among those players, Acuff is the signature talent. At 19 years old, he will be the starting point guard on opening night, able to run the offense and shoot his way through the inevitable growing pains without looking over his shoulder. Acuff has the keys, and Sacramento's current rebuild will be mostly judged through his growth arc. -- Slater

Biggest strength: The lack of immediate pressure. Perry's lone stated goal from an ESPN interview over the summer was to establish a tougher identity while eclipsing the 22-win mark from a season ago. Most experts are predicting the Kings as the worst team in the Western Conference. Local and internal expectations are a bit higher, but not by much. Thirty wins, especially if driven by their youth, would be viewed positively. There will certainly be some disappointing performances and home losses, but grander playoff demands are not hovering over this squad. -- Slater

Biggest weakness: The potential buy-in from a group of veterans that doesn't necessarily see a long-term future with the franchise. Perry has explored the trade market for Zach LaVine, Domantas Sabonis and Malik Monk in the past year. LaVine is on an expiring $48.9 million deal, which is viewed as Perry's first path to cap space and flexibility in the free agent market. Sabonis is extension-eligible, but there have been no discussions about adding to the two years and $94 million he has left. To recharge their value, LaVine and Sabonis will need productive stretches to open the season, but that can be a difficult ask on an ill-fitting roster for a team that is prioritizing development of more unproven players. -- Slater

Bold prediction: Acuff leads all rookies in points and all players in turnovers. Acuff should get all sorts of on-ball action this season; through his first two preseason games, for instance, his touch time was so high that it would have ranked in the top 10 in the league last season, per an analysis of GeniusIQ data. For a rookie guard, so much opportunity is a recipe for a large dose of high highs and low lows. -- Kram

Number to watch: 83. The Kings' five projected starters played just 83 combined games for the team last season. Sabonis, LaVine and Keegan Murray were injured for the majority of the campaign. De'Andre Hunter played just two games after a deadline trade before suffering an injury of his own. And Acuff, of course, was playing in college rather than Sacramento. -- Kram

Fantasy nugget: Acuff averaged 23.5 PPG and 6.4 APG at Arkansas, becoming the first SEC player since Pete Maravich to lead the conference in scoring and assists in the same season. Acuff is projected to start at point guard for Sacramento, giving him an immediate opportunity to produce. He is an appealing rookie target at his 104.4 ADP, particularly in points leagues, where inefficient shooting is less damaging. -- Moody

What Bobby Marks is watching: LaVine and Hunter. With their expiring contracts ($48.9 million and $24.9 million), Sacramento can unlock significant cap space in 2027. While a projected $50 million in room next summer looks appealing, should Sacramento consider trades now to bring back young players under contract for next season? In less than six months, Sacramento went from the fourth-oldest roster in the league to its 12th oldest, a boost in youth thanks to drafting Acuff, Alex Karaban and Emanuel Sharp in June.

BPI first-round projection: No. 1 (Note: The Kings also have San Antonio's 2027 first if it lands in the top 16.)

stories.headline: Antoine Semenyo out for two months, Man City hopeful over Erling Haaland
stories.summary: Antoine Semenyo is injured and faces an eight-week absence for Manchester City, Enzo Maresca confirmed.
stories.body:
Antoine Semenyo is injured and faces an eight-week absence for Manchester City, Enzo Maresca confirmed.

Erling Haaland, who suffered a knock at the weekend against Ipswich Town, is in the mix to play against AEK Athens on Tuesday in the Champions League.

Semenyo sustained a knee injury in City's 3-2 Premier League win over Ipswich, after he came off the bench in the 76th minute.

"After the scan we feel much better because it's not as bad as we expected," Maresca said about the Ghana winger.

"It could be eight weeks, so now the most important thing is for him to recover."

Semenyo, who arrived at City from Bournemouth last January, has scored two goals this season which both came last month against Sunderland.

In his absence, wide options available to Maresca include Iliman Ndiaye, Jérémy Doku, Phil Foden, Rayan Cherki and Allan.

Haaland was also limping after City beat Ipswich but Maresca was hopeful of an immediate return for him.

"He can be available," Maresca said. "We have a session now and we'll see."

Matheus Nunes, Mateo Kovacic, Nico O'Reilly also sustained knocks against Ipswich but Maresca doesn't fear an absence for that trio.

"They are, more or less, all okay," he said.

stories.headline: How Kimi Antonelli can win F1 title at United States GP -- with or without Qatar, Abu Dhabi races
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old, who has the potential to set a new record for the youngest Formula 1 champion this year, now leads Mercedes teammate Russell by 102 points in the standings with a maximum of 150 points still up for grabs.

The substantial lead means he could be crowned champion as early as Oct. 24 at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, but the maths around that calculation are slightly complicated by question marks over the final two races of the season. The grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are currently scheduled to go ahead on Nov. 29 and Dec. 6, but escalations in the war between the United States and Iran have the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

F1 has put a contingency plan in place to hold a single round at Imola if Qatar and Abu Dhabi are cancelled, but doing so would cut the championship short by one round and mean only 125 points are available to any single driver before the end of the year. Such a scenario would change the maths around the championship fight, making it easier for Antonelli to be crowned champion in Austin.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli, it's too late

- Verstappen takes back-to-back wins with dominant Singapore drive

- Hamilton calls Singapore strategy 'painful lesson' after Ferrari apology

Alongside Russell and Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris are still mathematically in contention for this year's championship, although the incredibly slim hopes of Leclerc and Norris would be snuffed out entirely by the cancellation of the races in the Middle East.

What does Antonelli need to do to be crowned champion in Austin?
Assuming the final two races go ahead as planned, Antonelli's chances of clinching the title in Austin remain relatively slim. The Mercedes driver would need to win in Texas, with his teammate Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing fifth or lower.

Such a scenario would put Antonelli 125 points ahead of Russell with 125 points remaining, but even if Antonelli failed to score another point and Russell won all the remaining rounds after Austin, Antonelli would still be crowned champion on countback of race victories (by that stage Antonelli would be on nine and Russell on three with five races remaining).

If the championship is shortened by the season ending in Imola rather than Abu Dhabi, Antonelli would only need to leave Austin with a lead of 100 points over his rivals.

Such a scenario would result in the following permutations:

If Antonelli wins in Austin he would be crowned champion regardless of where the others finish.
If Antonelli finishes second, he would be crowned champion if Russell doesn't win the race.
If Antonelli finishes third, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes off the podium.
If Antonelli finishes fourth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes behind him and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes fifth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fourth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes sixth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fifth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes seventh, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes sixth or lower and Hamilton does not finish in the top two.
If Antonelli finishes eighth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes seventh or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top two and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes ninth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes eighth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes tenth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli fails to score, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Verstappen does not win the race.

What's the minimum Antonelli needs to do be crowned champion?
Another way to look at the championship is the minimum amount of points Antonelli needs to score over the remaining rounds to secure the title regardless of what other drivers achieve. Assuming Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead, he needs 49 points over the remaining rounds, which could be achieved with as little as five sixth place finishes and one fifth place finish over the rest of the season.

If only five races remain, Antonelli would need just 24 points to secure the title, which would be attainable with two seventh place finishes and three eighth place finishes at the remaining rounds.
